title: Rewrite DNS dashboard to Nostr relay subscriptions (AGENTS.md violation)
description: web/src/routes/dns/+page.ts and dns.svelte.js fetch DNS data from REST endpoints and use a manual Refresh button. This violates AGENTS.md: 'If code is waiting and checking instead of subscribing and reacting, it is wrong.' Rewrite to subscribe to Kind 31976/31975 events via Nostr relay WebSocket. Remove REST fetches, remove Refresh button, make data update reactively.
notes: Implemented DNS dashboard long-lived Nostr relay subscription for Kind 31975/31976/31977/31978 read models; removed REST DNS data reads/manual refresh delivery; added deterministic EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH tests and PSTF verification. Final implementation does not use DNS REST fetches or queryUntilEose for dashboard data.
close_reason: Implemented DNS dashboard Nostr queryUntilEose bootstrap plus live relay subscriptions; removed REST DNS data reads/manual refresh delivery; added deterministic web tests and PSTF verification.

title: Remove REST DNS catalog layer (AGENTS.md violation)
description: dns_catalog.go, router DNS routes, and app.go DNSCatalog wiring expose DNS read-model data over HTTP GET endpoints. This violates AGENTS.md: 'Nostr is an event stream, not a request/response API.' The DNS projector already publishes Kind 31976 events. Remove the REST intermediary entirely.
close_reason: Closed

title: Validate Loom deployment completion events before mutating run state
description:
## Problem
The Loom deployment completion path currently trusts raw status/result events from relays. A forged, replayed, duplicate, or malformed Kind 30100/5101 event can drive deployment run state and worker stats without shared inbound validation, deduplication, or relay lifecycle handling.

## Evidence
- internal/workflow/coordinator.go: ExecuteDeployment starts pollForCompletion after SubmitJob and pollForCompletion maps c.loom.PollJobStatus result directly into CompleteDeploymentRun and recordJobStats.
- internal/adapters/loom/client.go: PollJobStatus subscribes to KindJobStatus/KindJobResult for #e=<jobEventID>, updates latest from ev.PubKey/tags/content, and returns parseJobResult(ev, jobEventID) with no ValidateInboundEvent/shared validation, no event-id dedup, and no explicit CLOSED/AUTH/EOSE handling.
- Existing bahia-5b4 covered protocol kind alignment and bahia-kua covered goroutine shutdown; neither tracks this exact trust/validation gap.

## Scope
Introduce a shared inbound Nostr event validation/dedup path for Loom job status/result handling and ensure relay CLOSED/AUTH/EOSE semantics are handled according to repository Nostr guardrails. Avoid request/response or polling-style substitutes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Loom status/result events are validated before use: event id, Schnorr signature, pubkey, timestamp bounds, required tags, expected kind, job correlation, and expected/selected worker where applicable.
- Duplicate event ids are ignored idempotently and do not double-count callbacks or worker stats.
- Subscription lifecycle handles CLOSED, AUTH, and EOSE explicitly; CLOSED/AUTH failures are surfaced and logged without trusting incomplete data.
- Tests deterministically inject EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH/duplicate/malformed events; no sleep-based event waiting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Forged, malformed, stale/future, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-job, and wrong-worker Loom events cannot complete a deployment run or update worker stats.
- Valid terminal Kind 5101 events still complete runs correctly.
- Tests cover relay CLOSED/AUTH/EOSE handling without sleeps.
notes: Related closed partials: bahia-5b4, bahia-kua.
close_reason: Fixed Loom completion polling validation/dedup/merged subscription handling and added deterministic tests; verified with go test ./internal/adapters/loom ./internal/workflow.

title: Scoped signer-first operator pubkeys are filtered out at reactor subscription boundary
description:
Problem
Scoped signer-first operator pubkeys for adoption and direct-runtime are authorized at runtime but filtered out before the reactor sees their events.

Evidence
- Oracle audit export: prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-05-16-165809-bahia-inheritance-au-3c11.md, Finding 1.
- internal/controlplane/reactor.go: requestSubscriptionAuthors() reads only Config.AuthorizedPubkeys.
- internal/controlplane/reactor.go: isAuthorizedFor() separately allows AdoptionAuthorizedPubkeys and DirectRuntimeAuthorizedPubkeys.
- Reactor.Run() currently builds one request filter for all request kinds, so relay-side author filtering can exclude scoped-only operators before validation/authorization/handler dispatch.
- docs/control-planes.md documents scoped signer-first operator authorization for adoption/direct-runtime flows.

Impact
- Valid 5978/5979 adoption requests from adoption-only operators can be dropped silently.
- Valid direct-runtime 5963 JSON action requests from direct-runtime-only operators can be dropped silently.
- No status/result/error/audit signal is produced because the event never crosses the subscription boundary.

Scope
- Do not broaden scoped allowlists into a single all-kinds author set.
- Split reactor request subscription filters by authorization scope: default/global, direct-runtime service action, and adoption requests.
- Preserve existing Nostr semantics: subscriptions, EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH handling, validation-before-dedup, no polling.
- Preserve the single since timestamp across reconnect/auth resubscribe paths.
- Add focused regression tests for filter construction and scoped-only operator configs.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Adoption-only pubkeys reach 5978/5979 reactor handlers without being added to AuthorizedPubkeys. 2. Direct-runtime-only pubkeys reach direct-runtime 5963 handling without being added to AuthorizedPubkeys. 3. Default request kinds remain relay-scoped to the global allowlist only. 4. Tests prove scope-aware filter construction, author union/deduplication, and unchanged EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH lifecycle behavior.
close_reason: Fixed scoped reactor subscription filters and added regression coverage; verified with go test ./internal/controlplane.

title: Reopen Cashu wallet: enabled payment service still has unsupported live token flows
description:
## Problem
Cashu payment wiring can be enabled, but the wallet adapter still returns unsupported errors for live token operations. A prior issue (`bahia-j7ww`) is closed, yet current app startup explicitly logs that live wallet token flows are not wired.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/cashu/wallet.go` validates balance/recipient, then returns `ErrMintBackedFlowUnsupported` instead of creating a payment token.
- `internal/adapters/cashu/wallet.go` `ReceiveToken` returns unsupported for non-empty tokens.
- `internal/app/app.go` enables `PaymentService` while warning live wallet token flows are not wired.

## Scope
- Either implement mint-backed send/receive/balance flows end-to-end, or fail closed when Cashu is configured as live.
- Replace tests that only assert placeholder/unsupported behavior with integration-contract tests against a real/fake mint boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Enabled Cashu mode performs real mint-backed token operations or startup fails with explicit unsupported-live-mode error.
- Payment API/CLI cannot present placeholder success.
- Tests cover success and mint rejection/error paths.
close_reason: Configured Cashu live mode now fails startup/config validation with an explicit unsupported mint-backed-flow error; payment handlers return 503 when service is unavailable and focused tests pass.

title: Fail closed when secret encryption is unavailable
description:
## Problem
Secret routes and encrypted handlers can be wired while the app has no Nostr private key/encryptor. Startup currently creates the encryptor only when `cfg.Nostr.PrivateKey` is present, but still passes secret repositories and possibly nil encryptor into router/control-plane wiring.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/app.go` creates the encryptor only under `cfg.Nostr.PrivateKey != ""`.
- Later app/router wiring still includes `Secrets: secretRepo` and encrypted route handlers with possibly nil `Encryptor`.

## Scope
- Decide whether secrets are disabled or startup fails when encryption is unavailable.
- Ensure secret create/reveal/mutate paths cannot store plaintext or silently degrade.
- Add tests for startup/router fail-closed behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Secret mutation/reveal paths are unavailable or fail startup without an encryptor.
- Error messages are explicit and no plaintext fallback is possible.
- Tests cover both configured and missing-encryptor cases.
close_reason: Implemented fail-closed secret encryption: encryptor construction rejects missing keys, HTTP create/update return 503 without encryptor, secret-dependent privileged config requires nostr.private_key, and focused tests pass.

title: Expose and handle relay CLOSED reasons, EOSE state, and subscription AUTH
description:
## Problem
Relay subscription plumbing hides protocol messages that callers need for event-driven correctness. `MergedSubscription` exposes events and EOSE only; CLOSED reasons and AUTH challenges are unavailable, and control-plane code cannot distinguish normal closure, auth-required, policy rejection, or rate limits.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/nostr/relay_pool.go` `MergedSubscription` has `Events` and `EndOfStoredEvents` but no CLOSED reason/AUTH channel.
- Subscription merge logic drops relay closure reasons and subscription errors.
- `internal/controlplane/reactor.go` subscribes via `SubscribeAllWithEOSE` but only selects on `merged.Events` and `ctx.Done()`, ignoring EOSE and lacking CLOSED/AUTH handling.

## Scope
- Extend relay subscription abstraction to surface CLOSED reason per relay/subscription and EOSE per relay.
- Implement NIP-42 subscription AUTH flow where relays require it.
- Update reactor/subscribers to log/handle CLOSED reasons and EOSE catch-up transitions.
- Add deterministic tests using mocked CLOSED, EOSE, AUTH, EVENT sequences.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CLOSED false/auth-required/rate-limit reasons are observable and handled.
- AUTH challenge flow signs kind 22242 with relay/challenge tags and retries appropriately.
- Reactor records/uses EOSE for historical catch-up rather than ignoring it.
- No tests rely on sleep to simulate relay protocol sequencing.
notes: Bucket 1 backend Go work implemented: MergedSubscription now surfaces per-relay EOSE and CLOSED metadata; Subscriber/Reactor log EOSE/CLOSED, attempt best-effort auth on auth-required closures, and resubscribe after successful auth. Focused Go tests passing. Left open pending broader acceptance review of AUTH challenge behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: Validate inbound Nostr events before persistence or dispatch
description:
## Problem
Inbound Nostr events are accepted at trust boundaries without NIP-01 validation. The generic subscriber records relay-provided events and dispatches handlers before verifying event ID/hash, Schnorr signature, pubkey/signature match, or timestamp bounds. Web relay clients also dispatch raw EVENT frames to UI consumers without validation.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/nostr/subscriber.go` builds and records `NostrEventRecord` before validation, then marks events seen and invokes handlers.
- `internal/adapters/nostr/subscriber_test.go` uses fake events with `Sig: "sig"` and invalid IDs as accepted inputs.
- `web/src/lib/nostr/client.js` parses `EVENT` frames and immediately invokes subscription callbacks with relay-provided event objects.

## Scope
- Add a shared inbound event validation path for Go subscriber/control-plane consumers.
- Reject or quarantine invalid events before persistence and handler dispatch.
- Add browser-side validation or explicit trusted-source gating before UI state updates from relay EVENT frames.
- Replace fake-event tests with signed valid events and explicit invalid-event rejection tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Invalid ID/signature/timestamp events are not persisted or dispatched.
- Tests cover valid signed events and each rejection reason.
- Web consumers do not receive unvalidated relay EVENT payloads, or the remaining exception is explicitly documented and fail-closed.
notes: Bucket 1 backend Go work implemented: shared ValidateInboundEvent before Subscriber persistence/dispatch and Reactor dispatch; signed/invalid backend tests added and passing. Not closing because issue acceptance also includes web client validation handled by concurrent sibling bucket.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace polling tool provisioning worker with event-driven processing
description:
## Problem
Tool provisioning currently violates the Nostr event-driven contract. `internal/app/background.go` runs `runToolProvisioningWorker` with a 10s ticker and calls `ProcessPendingIntents`, effectively polling repository state for work. `internal/controlplane/reactor.go` handles kind 5976 tool provision requests by creating an intent and publishing queued status, but does not hand the new intent to the coordinator immediately. This means real work depends on periodic polling rather than the request event and can be delayed or missed in tests that only assert queued behavior.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/background.go`: `runToolProvisioningWorker` uses `time.NewTicker(10 * time.Second)` to call `a.toolCoordinator.ProcessPendingIntents(ctx)`.
- `internal/app/app.go`: `Run` starts that worker with `go a.runToolProvisioningWorker(ctx)`.
- `internal/controlplane/reactor.go`: `handleToolProvisionRequest` creates a pending intent and returns after queued status. Approval responses do call `ProcessApprovedIntent`, so request handling should follow the same event-driven pattern.

## Scope
- Process a newly-created tool provisioning intent directly from the kind 5976 handler when a coordinator is configured.
- Remove the periodic app-level polling worker from normal runtime.
- Keep startup/recovery behavior explicit in a future issue if needed, not as a message-delivery loop.
- Add deterministic tests that prove the request handler advances beyond queued/pending without sleeps or tickers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No `time.NewTicker`/poll loop remains for tool provisioning message delivery.
- A valid kind 5976 request invokes coordinator processing directly.
- Tests verify event-driven processing and do not rely on sleeping for the 10s worker.
- Any remaining recovery/backfill need is separately tracked.
close_reason: Implemented event-driven processing for new kind 5976 tool provisioning requests, removed app-level 10s polling worker, added deterministic control-plane test, and verified with go test ./.... Follow-up recovery/serialization risks tracked separately as bahia-ph2r and bahia-h6st.

title: Remove Signet mock-mode success paths from production provisioning
description:
## Problem
The Signet/NIP-46 adapter silently enters "mock mode" when no bunker URI is configured. In that mode it provisions fake identities, signs with ephemeral local keys, and `SignAs()` can emit events with only `PubKey` set and no valid signature.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/signet/client.go`
  - `Connect()` logs a warning and marks the client connected when `bunkerURI == ""`.
  - `ProvisionAgent()` routes to `provisionAgentMock()`.
  - `SignAs()` in mock mode only sets `event.PubKey` and returns success.
- Soul Factory provisioning and profile publication depend on this client path.

## Why this matters
A production config omission turns remote signing into fake signing and can generate invalid Nostr events while the system reports success.

## Scope
- Remove or hard-gate mock mode from production/runtime codepaths.
- Make missing bunker configuration a hard failure for features that require Signet.
- Ensure `SignAs()` never returns success without a valid signature.
- Add tests for fail-closed behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Production provisioning/signing cannot proceed without a configured signer.
- No runtime path emits unsigned events while reporting success.
- Tests cover missing bunker config and real-signature requirements.
close_reason: Completed Bucket 1: Signet now fails closed without a bunker URI unless AllowMock is explicit, mock signing returns valid verifiable signatures with stored keys, and fail-closed/mock-mode regression tests cover provisioning, signing, SignAs, status, suspend/resume, revoke, and NIP-98.

title: Replace Cashu wallet placeholders with real mint-backed flow
description:
## Problem
The Cashu adapter is not a real wallet implementation. It fabricates funding quotes, creates local pseudo-tokens without mint swaps or NUT-10 locking, accepts incoming proofs without mint verification, and keeps wallet state only in memory. `app.New()` also enables `PaymentService` without wiring a real `cashu.Wallet`, so "Cashu enabled" does not produce real ecash behavior.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/cashu/wallet.go`
  - `CreateMintQuote()` returns `"lnbc<amount>..."` placeholder text instead of POSTing to `/v1/mint/quote/bolt11`.
  - `CreatePaymentToken()` never swaps proofs with the mint and comments explicitly describe missing production behavior.
  - `ReceiveToken()` trusts token contents and adds proofs directly, with no mint-side verification/double-spend protection.
- Wallet balances/proofs are in-memory maps only.
- `internal/app/app.go` instantiates `PaymentService` but never constructs or injects a `cashu.Wallet`.

## Why this matters
Payments can appear supported while being non-redeemable, non-verifiable, and non-persistent. That is production-fake behavior around money.

## Scope
- Decide and implement the real Cashu mint interactions required for mint quotes, swaps, proof verification, and change handling.
- Persist wallet state or explicitly integrate with a real wallet backend.
- Wire the wallet into app/runtime flows so payment-enabled configs actually exercise the adapter.
- Replace mock-only tests with integration-style adapter tests against HTTP mint fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quote creation calls a real mint API.
- Outbound payment tokens are mint-issued/locked, not local JSON blobs.
- Incoming tokens are verified/redeemed with the mint.
- App wiring uses the wallet when Cashu is enabled.
close_reason: Bucket 2 hardening complete: Soul Factory fake surfaces fail explicitly, Cashu fake token paths gated, and qdrant/agent-memory unsafe defaults removed.

title: Fail closed on empty Nostr control-plane allowlist
description:
## Problem
`internal/controlplane/reactor.go` grants control-plane access to a built-in fallback list of developer pubkeys whenever `config.AuthorizedPubkeys` is empty. In a production deploy with missing or partial config, deploy/rollback/service-create/LLM control silently remains open to those keys.

## Evidence
- `DefaultAuthorizedPubkeys` contains two hardcoded pubkeys in `internal/controlplane/reactor.go`.
- `isAuthorized()` replaces an empty configured allowlist with that fallback.
- `app.New()` wires `cfg.Nostr.AuthorizedPubkeys` directly into the reactor without validating that production config actually sets it.

## Why this matters
This is an authorization fail-open path for the Nostr control plane. A config omission becomes a privilege grant.

## Scope
- Remove the hardcoded fallback from the reactor runtime path.
- Fail closed when no authorized pubkeys are configured.
- Add a regression test proving unauthorized access when config is empty.
- Consider startup/config validation or prominent logging so operators catch misconfiguration early.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reactor never authorizes a pubkey unless it is explicitly configured.
- Tests cover explicit allowlist success and empty-allowlist failure.
- No production path depends on embedded developer keys.
close_reason: Completed: reactor now rejects all pubkeys when AuthorizedPubkeys is empty, embedded developer-key fallback removed, and regression tests cover explicit allowlist success vs empty-allowlist denial.

description: When reconnection fails, the loop immediately hits the closed channel again with only a fixed 5s pause. The existing Backoff struct in nostr/backoff.go should be used for exponential backoff. Fix: use nostrpool.DefaultBackoff() with Next()/Reset() pattern
close_reason: Fixed: publishError tag, slice mutation, unauthorized error, backoff reconnect, signature verification, event deduplication, entity validation, runtime_type validation

title: [Bug] Reactor handleServiceAction silently drops unauthorized requests
description: handleServiceAction only logs unauthorized requests but doesn't publish an error event. Every other handler calls publishError on auth failure. Fix: add r.publishError call before returning

description: append(config.Relays, config.PrivateRelays...) may mutate the caller's slice backing array. Fix: copy first with make() then append both slices
close_reason: Fixed: publishError tag, slice mutation, unauthorized error, backoff reconnect, signature verification, event deduplication, entity validation, runtime_type validation

description: publishError uses step instead of message in the error tag. The error tag should contain the human-readable error description, not the step identifier. Fix: change {'error', step} to {'error', message}

title: [Docker Runtime] Add volume mount support to Deploy()
description: CRITICAL: DeployOptions has no Volumes field and Deploy() sends no Binds in HostConfig. Stateful services lose data. Fix: Add Volumes []string field, parse in Deploy(), add to hostConfig[Binds].

description: CRITICAL: DockerObserver.Deploy() never reads Ports field from DeployOptions. hostConfig has only RestartPolicy, no PortBindings. Containers get no published ports. Fix: Parse opts.Ports into Docker API format, add ExposedPorts on container config and PortBindings on host config.

description: CRITICAL: deployCommands() creates deployCmd and rollbackCmd but never adds them as subcommands. Function returns bare cobra.Command with no children. These commands are unreachable dead code. Fix: Add parent.AddCommand(deployCmd, rollbackCmd) before return.

title: Deployment approval is bypassable - no guard on intent state transitions
description:
## Problem
The deployment intent state machine has no guards. For example:

1. ApproveDeploymentIntent doesn't check if the intent is in 'pending' approval state - you can approve an already-rejected intent
2. CreateDeploymentRun doesn't verify the intent is approved before creating a run
3. CompleteDeploymentRun doesn't verify the run is in 'running' or 'queued' state
4. There's no transition validation anywhere - any status can transition to any other status

## Evidence
ApproveDeploymentIntent (registry.go:289): checks intent exists but not its current approval_status or status
RejectDeploymentIntent (registry.go:307): no state checks at all
CreateDeploymentRun (registry.go:313): no check that intent is approved

## Impact
Protected environments with approval requirements can be bypassed by directly creating deployment runs for pending/rejected intents.

## Required Fix
- Add state machine validation for intent status transitions
- Verify intent is in approved state before allowing run creation
- Reject approve/reject on already-terminal intents
- Add comprehensive state transition tests
close_reason: Added state transition guards: ApproveIntent checks pending approval status, RejectIntent checks pending status, CreateRun verifies intent is approved/deploying, CompleteRun validates terminal status and rejects already-completed runs. Added 8 tests verifying all guards.

title: Rollback logic is broken - rolls back to current state, not previous
description:
## Problem
The Rollback method in `internal/service/registry.go:408-455` has a critical logic bug:

```go
intents, err := s.intents.ListByServiceEnv(ctx, serviceID, envID, 2, 0)
if err != nil || len(intents) < 2 {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("no previous deployment to roll back to")
}
previousArtifactID := intents[1].ArtifactID
```

The list is ordered by `created_at DESC`. So intents[0] is the CURRENT intent and intents[1] is the PREVIOUS. However, the method first fetches the last successful run's intent separately, then fetches the top-2 intents. If there was a failed deployment between the current and last-successful, intents[1] may point to the FAILED deployment's artifact, not the last-known-good one.

Additionally, after creating the rollback intent via CreateDeploymentIntent, it triggers the state upsert which overwrites DesiredArtifactID. But the method doesn't verify the previous artifact still exists in the registry.

## Impact
Rollbacks may deploy a broken artifact instead of the last-known-good one.

## Required Fix
- Use LastSuccessfulRunID -> intent -> artifact chain instead of latest-2 heuristic
- Verify the rollback target artifact still exists
- Add tests covering the failed-deployment-between scenario
close_reason: Fixed rollback to walk intent history looking for the most recent successfully-deployed intent with a different artifact than current. Validates target artifact still exists. Skips failed intents. Added 3 rollback tests covering happy path, failed-intent-between, and no-history cases.

title: Auth middleware is a complete no-op even when enabled
description:
## Problem
The auth middleware in `internal/auth/auth.go` is entirely fake. When `enabled=true`, the middleware accepts ALL requests without any JWT validation. The TODO on line 19 says 'Implement JWT validation when auth is enabled' but the code just calls `next.ServeHTTP(w, r)` unconditionally.

## Evidence
Line 19-20 of auth.go: The handler just passes through regardless of the enabled flag being true.

## Impact
**CRITICAL SECURITY**: Any API consumer can perform any action (create deployments, delete services, rollback) with zero authentication. The config exposes auth.enabled and auth.jwt_secret giving operators false confidence.

## Required Fix
- Parse JWT from Authorization header (Bearer token)
- Validate signature against configured secret
- Extract claims and attach to request context
- Return 401 for missing/invalid tokens
- Add tests that verify rejection of bad tokens and acceptance of valid ones
close_reason: Implemented real JWT HMAC-SHA256 auth with ValidateToken, GenerateToken, fail-closed behavior, context propagation, and 11 comprehensive tests. Wired into router for /api/v1 routes.

title: Handle web Nostr EOSE queries across relay reconnects
description:
## Problem
Bahia web dashboard and routes stop showing events when the configured relay disconnects/reconnects before one-shot bootstrap/profile queries receive EOSE. The browser console shows NostrIncompleteEOSEError: relays closed before all EOSE messages were received after reconnect to wss://bahia.sharegap.net/relay.

## Observed behavior
The app connects, a relay closes during kind-0/control-plane bootstrap, queryUntilEose rejects as all_relays_closed, and bootstrap paths do not recover to resubscribe after reconnect.

## Intended behavior
Historical bootstrap queries remain EOSE-authoritative but must be reconnect-aware: relay closure should be surfaced explicitly, then bootstrap should retry by reissuing scoped REQ subscriptions after reconnect instead of leaving routes empty. No timeout-based completion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Web bootstrap/profile query paths recover after relay reconnect by issuing fresh scoped subscriptions and waiting for EOSE.
- CLOSED before EOSE remains an incomplete history failure for that subscription attempt and is logged/handled explicitly.
- Tests deterministically inject EVENT, EOSE, CLOSED, and connection changes without sleeps.
- PSTF artifacts record observed behavior, acceptance criteria, test mapping, and verification evidence.
notes: Implemented reconnect-aware EOSE query behavior in web Nostr client. Transport close before EOSE is non-terminal for historical queries; scoped subscriptions remain active and are reissued on reconnect. Relay CLOSED frames and exhausted reconnect attempts still reject with NostrIncompleteEOSEError. Verification: pnpm --dir web exec vitest run --config vitest.config.js tests/unit/sanity.test.js tests/unit/nostr-client-parsing.test.js (49 passed); broader gate with test-utils/controlplane-requests also passed (59 passed). PSTF WEB_NOSTR_VALIDATION_EOSE updated.
close_reason: Fixed reconnect-aware browser Nostr EOSE bootstrap handling; verified with focused and broader web Nostr unit gates; PSTF WEB_NOSTR_VALIDATION_EOSE updated.

title: Attribute secret creation audits to authenticated principal
description:
## Problem
Secret creation records hardcode CreatedBy to the literal string "api" even though the route requires write-secret permission. Audit records therefore cannot identify which authenticated user/principal created a secret.

## Evidence
- internal/api/handlers/secrets.go: Create calls requirePermission(PermWriteSecrets) but constructs domain.ServiceSecret with CreatedBy: "api" and a TODO to extract from auth context.
- toSecretRefResponse exposes created_by, so clients receive the non-attributable value.
- Existing bahia-dga implemented secrets management and bahia-00vf fixed fail-closed encryption; neither tracks authenticated audit attribution.

## Scope
Resolve the authenticated principal from request/auth context and persist it in ServiceSecret.CreatedBy for creates. Preserve fail-closed authorization behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CreatedBy for new secrets is derived from the authenticated principal, not a static string.
- Missing/ambiguous principal on a write-secret request fails closed or records an explicit, policy-approved system principal only where appropriate.
- API response and repository state expose the authenticated creator.
- Tests cover authenticated user attribution and missing-principal behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Creating a secret as principal A stores and returns created_by=A.
- A write-secret request with permission but no resolvable principal cannot silently store created_by="api".
- Existing encryption fail-closed tests continue to pass.
notes: Related closed partials: bahia-dga, bahia-00vf.
close_reason: Implemented authenticated principal attribution for secret creation; missing principal now fails closed with 401 before persistence; focused handler tests pass.

title: Reactor outbound event auditing must not depend on packages feature flag
description:
Problem
Reactor outbound event auditing is accidentally tied to the packages feature flag.

Evidence
- Oracle audit export: prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-05-16-165809-bahia-inheritance-au-3c11.md, Finding 3.
- internal/app/app.go only appends controlplane.WithNostrEventRepository(nostrEventRepo) inside the packageRegistrySvc != nil composition branch.
- internal/controlplane/reactor.go publishEvent() records outbound events only when r.nostrEvents is non-nil.

Impact
- Outbound deployment/action/LLM/adoption/tool/assistant control-plane events are not audited in deployments where packages are disabled.
- An unrelated package feature toggle changes generic control-plane audit behavior.

Scope
- Always inject nostrEventRepo into the reactor when the repository exists.
- Keep package-specific service injection separate from generic outbound event auditing.
- Add composition coverage for package-enabled and package-disabled configurations.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Outbound control-plane events are audited whenever nostrEventRepo exists, regardless of package feature state. 2. Package enablement changes only package-specific behavior, not generic reactor event auditing. 3. Tests or integration assertions cover package-enabled and package-disabled app composition.
close_reason: Wired reactor Nostr event repository independently of package feature state, added package-enabled/disabled composition coverage, and passed go test ./internal/adapters/nostr ./internal/app

title: Converge Hive-CI subscriber on shared inbound validation and relay-closure contract
description:
Problem
The Hive-CI subscriber implements a parallel weaker Nostr trust boundary and does not fully consume merged relay lifecycle metadata.

Evidence
- Oracle audit export: prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-05-16-165809-bahia-inheritance-au-3c11.md, Finding 4.
- internal/adapters/hiveci/subscriber.go handleEvent() calls ev.CheckSignature() only, not the shared adapters/nostr ValidateInboundEvent(...).
- The subscription loop does not handle RelayEOSE and Closed metadata consistently with the primary Subscriber/Reactor paths.

Impact
- Events with malformed IDs, timestamp abuse, or kind/tag-structure defects may cross this boundary if they only pass signature checks.
- Relay CLOSED/AUTH/debug behavior diverges from the rest of Bahia's Nostr stack.

Scope
- Run shared ValidateInboundEvent(...) before Hive-CI parse/persist/dispatch.
- Handle or observe RelayEOSE and Closed messages consistently with the shared relay/subscriber contract.
- Implement deterministic tests with injected EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED behavior; do not add sleep-based tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Invalid inbound Hive-CI events are dropped before persistence or dispatch using shared ValidateInboundEvent semantics. 2. Relay CLOSED/AUTH-required conditions are observable and retried or handled where configured. 3. Per-relay EOSE/CLOSED behavior is covered by deterministic tests without sleeps.
close_reason: Completed Hive-CI subscriber parity: shared ValidateInboundEvent before parse/persist/dispatch; deterministic RelayEOSE/CLOSED handling; auth-required CLOSED authenticates once and immediately resubscribes with same filters. Verified with go test ./internal/adapters/hiveci.

title: Complete canonical control-plane inbound audit coverage in generic Nostr subscriber
description:
Problem
The generic Nostr subscriber's inbound audit coverage does not match the canonical control-plane request namespace documented and handled elsewhere.

Evidence
- Oracle audit export: prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-05-16-165809-bahia-inheritance-au-3c11.md, Finding 2.
- internal/adapters/nostr/subscriber.go DefaultInboundKinds omits 5971-5975 LLM request kinds, 5978-5979 adoption request kinds, and 5981-5989 public signed write/evaluate kinds.
- docs/control-planes.md and reactor handling describe a broader canonical namespace.
- Current author scoping is a single flattened pubkey set rather than scope-aware request filters.

Impact
- nostr_events inbound audit coverage is incomplete.
- Replay, debug, and historical investigation tools cannot rely on subscriber persistence for the complete control-plane contract.
- Scoped request audit parity may require widening filters unless explicitly grouped.

Scope
- Align DefaultInboundKinds with the canonical documented/handled namespace or document explicit exclusions.
- Add scope-aware author filtering where needed so audit coverage does not widen unrelated relay filters.
- Preserve the subscriber's existing validation-before-persist behavior and EOSE/CLOSED handling.
- Add tests locking the final kind map and filter composition.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Subscriber inbound kind coverage matches the canonical control-plane namespace or every exclusion is documented with rationale. 2. Scoped request kinds are audited without widening unrelated author filters. 3. Tests lock the final kind map and filter composition. 4. Existing validation-before-persist and event-driven EOSE/CLOSED behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Implemented canonical inbound audit kind coverage, scoped subscriber author filters, deterministic tests, and passed go test ./internal/adapters/nostr ./internal/app

title: Serialize tool provisioning per service/environment target
description:
## Problem
Tool provisioning work can now be triggered concurrently by multiple Nostr request handler goroutines, and approval handling already invoked `ProcessApprovedIntent` inline. The coordinator does not visibly serialize processing per `(service_id, environment_id)`, so overlapping toolset deployments can race image deployment and profile-state updates.

## Evidence
- `internal/controlplane/reactor.go` dispatches request handlers in goroutines and calls the coordinator directly.
- `internal/service/tool_provisioning_coordinator.go` updates `ToolProfileState.PreviousImageDigest` and `CurrentImageDigest` without per-target locking.

## Scope
- Add coordinator-side locking/queueing keyed by service/environment.
- Ensure separate targets can process concurrently while the same target is serialized.
- Add deterministic concurrency tests around profile-state ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two intents for the same service/environment cannot deploy/update profile state concurrently.
- Intents for different targets can still run independently.
- Tests prove `PreviousImageDigest`/`CurrentImageDigest` remains consistent under concurrent requests.
close_reason: Implemented per service/environment serialization with deterministic concurrency/profile-state tests.

title: Add explicit durable recovery for stranded tool provisioning intents
description:
## Problem
After replacing the periodic tool provisioning poller with event-driven request processing, persisted intents still need an explicit recovery path. Nostr request subscriptions use current-time filters and should not be treated as durable replay queues. If Bahia crashes after `CreateIntent`, or processing fails transiently before a terminal state, stored `pending`/`approved` intents can remain stranded unless recovery is explicit.

## Evidence
- `internal/controlplane/reactor.go` now processes newly-created kind 5976 intents inline from the request event.
- `internal/service/tool_provisioning_coordinator.go` still has `ProcessPendingIntents`, but normal runtime no longer uses a periodic ticker.
- Reactor subscriptions are scoped to current time, so old request events are not replayed for recovery.

## Scope
- Add a startup/resume recovery mechanism for stored non-terminal tool provisioning intents that is clearly separate from message-delivery polling.
- Define retry/backoff semantics for transient failures without using polling to detect new events.
- Add deterministic tests for restart/recovery of `pending` and `approved` intents.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Newly-arrived requests are event-triggered; recovery of stored work is explicit and documented.
- Stranded `pending`/`approved` intents are retried on startup/resume.
- Recovery tests do not use sleeps or ticker timing.
close_reason: Implemented explicit tool provisioning recovery runner, startup recovery coverage, and pending/approved recovery tests.

title: Handle Blossom auth-header failures explicitly on read/proxy paths
description:
## Problem
Blossom read/proxy paths silently ignore errors when creating NIP-98/auth headers. Private/auth-required blob operations may proceed unauthenticated and fail later as ambiguous upstream errors.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/blossom/download.go` drops `createAuthHeader` errors on download.
- `internal/adapters/blossom/proxy.go` drops auth errors on HEAD and GET stream paths.

## Scope
- Return explicit auth-preparation errors for private/auth-required requests.
- Decide whether public reads can proceed unauthenticated and document that branch.
- Add tests for auth header construction failure and relay/storage rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Auth header generation failures are not silently swallowed for protected operations.
- Error responses identify auth preparation vs upstream blob failure.
- Tests prove no unauthenticated fallback occurs when auth is required.
close_reason: Implemented explicit Blossom auth-header failure propagation for read/proxy paths, 503 handler mapping, and regression tests proving no unauthenticated fallback. Focused touched-package tests reported ok; overall go test command is blocked by unrelated concurrent internal/adapters/nostr compile mismatch.

title: Replace remaining sleep-based and helper-only tests with deterministic behavior proofs
description:
## Problem
Several tests still rely on wall-clock sleeps or assert only helper/mock behavior. Some prior issues that claimed to replace fake tests are closed, but brittle tests remain. This weakens CI as production proof.

## Evidence
- `internal/events/events_async_test.go` uses handler sleep plus `time.After`.
- `internal/api/middleware/ratelimit_test.go` sleeps for token refill and cleanup.
- `internal/service/registry_test.go` sleeps for async publish and rollback ordering.
- `web/tests/unit/sanity.test.js` asserts `true` and arithmetic/browser globals.
- `web/tests/unit/test-utils-and-fixtures.test.js` mainly tests mock helpers/fixture shape.

## Scope
- Replace sleeps with injected clocks, channels, or deterministic callback synchronization.
- Strengthen assertions to verify event type, payload, correlation IDs, and state transitions.
- Remove or demote sanity/helper-only tests so coverage reports do not imply product behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No listed tests use sleeps to wait for behavior.
- Async behavior tests use deterministic synchronization.
- Product behavior assertions replace helper-only confidence where feasible.
notes:
Bucket 5 backend portion: replaced sleeps in internal/events/events_async_test.go with channel handshakes and ratelimit_test.go with fake clock/direct cleanup seam. Web and other listed non-bucket tests remain for sibling/follow-up work.
Bucket 2 web portion implemented: replaced web sanity/helper-only tests with deterministic behavior coverage for browser Nostr validation, EOSE completion, incomplete query errors, branch fail-closed behavior, and control-plane CLOSED/auth errors. Backend listed tests remain separate sibling scope, so issue stays open.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add auth support and fail-closed behavior to Qdrant adapter
description:
## Problem
The Qdrant adapter only accepts URL and timeout configuration and sends JSON requests without API-key/auth headers. This makes the integration unusable with secured Qdrant deployments or encourages unauthenticated vector stores.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/qdrant/client.go` config contains only `URL` and `Timeout`.
- Collection/upsert/search request construction sets content-type but no API key or auth header.

## Scope
- Add API-key/header configuration for Qdrant.
- Ensure auth headers are attached to every request.
- Add tests proving secured-server interactions and rejection/misconfiguration behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Config can supply Qdrant API key or explicit auth header.
- All Qdrant HTTP requests include configured auth.
- Missing auth can be explicitly allowed only for local/dev mode; production config fails closed.
close_reason: Added Qdrant API key/header configuration, centralized authenticated request creation for every operation, fail-closed missing-auth behavior with explicit local unauthenticated escape hatch, and focused tests pass.

title: Replace web Nostr timeout-based query completion with EOSE-driven flow
description:
## Problem
The browser Nostr client still resolves historical queries using wall-clock timeouts. This can treat missing events as complete history and violates the repo guardrail that backfill completion must be driven by EOSE, not "no events after N ms".

## Evidence
- `web/src/lib/nostr/client.js` `query(filters, timeout=5000)` resolves collected events from `setTimeout` even if EOSE has not arrived from all relays.
- `web/src/lib/nostr/branches.js` uses this query path for repository state.

## Scope
- Track per-relay EOSE for query subscriptions.
- Resolve only when expected relay EOSEs arrive, or when caller explicitly cancels via AbortSignal/user timeout that is not interpreted as complete history.
- Update tests to inject EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Query completion is EOSE-driven.
- Timeout/cancel paths return a distinct incomplete/cancelled error, not partial successful results.
- Branch/repository consumers handle incomplete history fail-closed or show an explicit degraded state.
close_reason: Implemented web Nostr EOSE-authoritative query completion. query/queryUntilEose now resolve only on all-relay EOSE and reject timeout/abort/closed-incomplete with NostrIncompleteEOSEError; branch consumers fail closed. Verified with targeted web unit tests.

title: Remove hardcoded LLM avatar backend default and placeholder provider advertisement
description:
## Problem
The LLM avatar adapter has production-facing hardcoded and placeholder behavior. If config omits an avatar backend URL, the code defaults to a private LAN ComfyUI endpoint. It also registers unavailable placeholder providers (`fal`, `replicate`) as provider entries.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/llm/avatar.go` defaults `LemmyURL` to `http://192.168.30.10:8188`.
- The avatar provider registry registers `fal` and `replicate` as unavailable placeholder providers.

## Scope
- Remove private-network default URL from production code.
- Require explicit configured provider endpoint for live generation.
- Hide unavailable providers from production capability lists or mark them as disabled config entries that cannot be selected.
- Add tests for missing config fail-closed behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No hardcoded developer/private network endpoint is used by default.
- Selecting an unconfigured provider fails validation before runtime request handling.
- Capability output does not imply placeholder providers are live.
close_reason: Removed the hardcoded private-network avatar backend default and default placeholder provider registration; generator now advertises only configured providers and fails closed for missing/unconfigured providers with focused tests passing.

title: Implement SBOM support as Nostr-first attestation/index feature
description:
## Goal
Implement SBOM support in Bahia that:
- Uses SPDX and CycloneDX as accepted payload formats (no proprietary format)
- Uses in-toto/SLSA-style attestations for provenance
- Uses NIP-51-style parameterized lists as the public index of SBOMs
- Uses Blossom/OCI/package-backend adapters for blob storage (not Nostr)
- Adds policy checks for SBOM presence, parseability, subject digest match, NTIA minimum fields, and trusted generator identity

## Design Principles
1. Do NOT make Nostr carry large SBOM payloads
2. Do NOT require one vendor backend
3. Do NOT build a proprietary SBOM format

## Components
1. **Domain Models**: SBOMAttestation, SBOMIndex event types
2. **SBOM Attestation Adapter**: in-toto style attestation wrapper
3. **SBOM Index Publisher**: NIP-51-style parameterized list events
4. **Storage Adapters**: Blossom + OCI referrers + package backend
5. **Policy Rules**: NTIA minimum fields, trusted generator, subject digest match
6. **Nostr Event Kinds**: New replaceable list kind for SBOM indexes
close_reason: Implemented SBOM Nostr-first attestation/index feature with in-toto/SLSA-style attestations, NIP-51-style parameterized list indexes, multi-backend storage (Blossom/OCI/package), and new SBOM policy rules (subject digest match, parseability, NTIA min fields, trusted generator, format)

title: Correct signature verification semantics for Nostr and cosign adapters
description:
## Problem
Nostr/cosign verification semantics are misleading: the Nostr verifier cannot proactively verify signatures for an artifact, and the cosign verifier marks registry presence as `Verified: true` without cryptographic validation.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/signing/nostr_sign.go` returns `nil, nil` from `VerifySignatures()` and calls it a no-op.
- `internal/adapters/signing/cosign.go` sets `Verified: true` when a matching referrer exists in the registry.

## Why this matters
Policy evaluation can treat unverified or only-discovered attestations as trusted security signals.

## Scope
- Tighten semantics so `Verified` only means cryptographically verified.
- Distinguish "discovered" from "validated" signatures in returned records.
- Add policy tests proving unverifiable signatures do not satisfy enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Security policy cannot be satisfied by mere registry presence.
- Signature-verification APIs expose truthful verification state.
close_reason: Completed Bucket 5: added signature verification status, migrated persistence, made cosign discovery unverified, set explicit Nostr verified/rejected statuses, updated API counts and policy tests.

title: Remove hardcoded LAN defaults from Qdrant and agent-memory adapters
description:
## Problem
Multiple adapters fall back to hardcoded private LAN service URLs when config is missing.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/qdrant/client.go` defaults to `http://192.168.40.104:6333`.
- `internal/adapters/agentmemory/client.go` defaults to `http://192.168.40.104:8282`.

## Why this matters
A production misconfiguration can silently direct traffic to a developer workstation address or simply fail with unreachable private-network endpoints.

## Scope
- Remove hardcoded private-network defaults.
- Require explicit configuration or safe localhost/dev-only gating.
- Add tests covering missing-config behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Production adapters do not embed developer LAN addresses.
- Missing required URLs fail clearly.
close_reason: Bucket 2 hardening complete: Soul Factory fake surfaces fail explicitly, Cashu fake token paths gated, and qdrant/agent-memory unsafe defaults removed.

title: Fix Nostr reconnect backfill and weak subscription scoping
description:
## Problem
The Nostr subscriber and related subscription helpers do not provide real reconnect backfill and use weak, kind-only filters. On reconnect the subscriber asks for events `Since: now`, so events from the disconnect window are dropped while `caughtUp` still flips after EOSE.

## Evidence
- `internal/adapters/nostr/subscriber.go` builds filters with `Kinds: s.kinds, Since: nowTimestamp()`.
- `backfillLimit` is effectively inert with `Since: now`.
- `Publisher.Subscribe()` uses kind-only filters without EOSE-aware subscriptions.
- Nostr audit also found partial EOSE coverage and multi-relay gaps.

## Why this matters
Command/result events can be missed across reconnects, and broad filters can over-consume relay traffic or mix unrelated workloads.

## Scope
- Track last-seen timestamps/positions for reconnect backfill.
- Use scoped filters where possible (`#p`, task tags, etc.).
- Upgrade relevant subscription helpers to EOSE-aware variants.
- Add deterministic tests covering reconnect backfill and EOSE transitions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Subscriber replays the disconnect window instead of dropping it.
- Filters are scoped to the intended workload where protocol permits.
- Tests cover reconnect + EOSE behavior without sleeps.
close_reason: Completed Bucket 4: reconnect subscriptions now use persisted/in-memory per-scope cursors with overlap; command filters are author-scoped where configured; repository inserts report duplicate-vs-new; handlers run only for newly inserted events; EOSE merge tests are deterministic.

title: Replace fake sleep-based Nostr/event tests with deterministic coverage
description:
## Problem
Several tests are fake or timing-based instead of proving real event behavior. This includes sleep-based async tests and a vacuous subscriber caught-up test that never touches the real atomic state or an actual EOSE transition.

## Evidence
- `internal/events/events_test.go` uses `time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)` three times to wait for handler execution.
- `internal/adapters/nostr/protocol_frames_test.go` asserts local booleans instead of exercising `Subscriber.caughtUp`.
- Repo review also found broad mock-only patterns in Soul Factory and web E2E coverage.

## Why this matters
These tests can pass while the production event flow is broken or flaky, especially around async sequencing.

## Scope
- Replace timing waits with `WaitGroup`/channels.
- Replace vacuous EOSE/caught-up checks with real stateful tests.
- Prefer deterministic relay/event fixtures over sleeps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No sleep-based waits remain in the touched Nostr/event unit tests.
- Subscriber caught-up logic is tested through real code paths.
- Tests fail if event delivery or EOSE handling regresses.
close_reason: Completed: replaced sleep-based waits in internal/events tests with WaitGroups and replaced the vacuous subscriber caught-up test with deterministic coverage over Subscriber state transitions.

title: Replace Soul Factory mock/no-op surfaces with real behavior or explicit gating
description:
## Problem
Soul Factory surfaces appear implemented but are mostly mock/no-op behavior. The CLI, MCP server, and provisioner return hardcoded data, fake progress, skipped steps, and success messages without actually querying relays or driving real provisioning/deployment.

## Evidence
- `cmd/cli/soulfactory.go` returns hardcoded souls/templates, simulates progress with `time.Sleep`, and lifecycle commands only print success.

title: Implement LookupRepositoryCI in pg_hiveci.go
description:
Implement batch CI lookup query in the Postgres repository.

## Query Strategy

Use **two SQL queries + Go-side assembly**:

### Query 1: Latest run + result per coordinate
- Use CTE over requested coordinate array
- DISTINCT ON or window function to pick latest run per repo_coordinate
- Order by event_created_at DESC, created_at DESC, run_event_id DESC
- LEFT JOIN hiveci_workflow_results ON run_event_id
- Returns one row per coordinate with run + result data

### Query 2: Policies + service/environment names
- Query hiveci_pipeline_policies for all requested coordinates
- JOIN services ON service_id
- JOIN environments ON environment_id
- Filter: enabled=true unless includeDisabledPolicies
- Build Policies slice and aggregate LinkedServices by (repo_coordinate, service_id)

### Assembly
- Build map keyed by repo_coordinate
- Return slice in request's first-seen order
- Coordinates with no data get empty result entries

## Edge Cases
- Orphaned results (pending_run without run) are not returned
- Duplicate coordinates in request: dedupe, don't duplicate output
- Policies with no runs: still return valid result entry

## Files
- internal/repository/pg_hiveci.go (modify)

## Dependencies
- Requires RepositoryCILookup types
- Requires interface method signature

## Done when
- LookupRepositoryCI method fully implemented
- Returns correct data for all edge cases
- Preserves request coordinate order
- Handles empty/no-data coordinates gracefully

title: Add service repository validation in handlers
description:
Add request validation and mapping logic in services.go for the compatibility matrix.

## Compatibility Matrix - Create

| Input | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| repo_url only | Accept; synthesize repository |
| repository only with clone_url | Accept; derive repo_url |
| repository only without clone_url | Reject 400 |
| both present and equal | Accept; canonicalize from repository |
| both present and different | Reject 400 |
| neither present | Accept; no repository |

## Compatibility Matrix - Update

| Input | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| omit both | Leave existing unchanged |
| repo_url only non-empty | Update; replace repository with synthesized |
| repo_url only empty string | Clear both |
| repository only with clone_url | Update; derive repo_url |
| repository only without clone_url | Reject 400 |
| both present and equal | Accept |
| both present and different | Reject 400 |
| repo_url="" plus non-empty repository | Reject 400 (contradictory) |

## Validation Rules
- repository.source allowed: "manual", "nip34", or omitted
- repository.repo_coordinate required when source="nip34"
- repository.clone_url required when repository is used to set value
- repository.relay_urls: trim and dedupe
- repository.ci.provider allowed: omitted or "hiveci"
- repository.ci.workflow_path: non-empty after trim if present

## Implementation
Add private validation helper(s) in services.go that:
1. Validate request according to rules above
2. Return 400 with clear error message on violations
3. Map validated request to domain.Service

## Files
- internal/api/handlers/services.go (modify)

## Done when
- Create handler validates and maps repository field
- Update handler validates and maps repository field
- All compatibility matrix cases return correct status codes
- Error messages clearly indicate the validation failure

title: Add services.repository JSONB migration
description:
Add database migration for structured repository column on services table.

## Migration Files

### 000015_services_repository_ref.up.sql
```sql
-- Add nullable JSONB column for structured repository metadata
ALTER TABLE services
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS repository JSONB;

-- Backfill legacy rows with repo_url into repository object
UPDATE services
SET repository = jsonb_build_object(
  'source', 'manual',
  'clone_url', repo_url
)
WHERE (repo_url IS NOT NULL AND repo_url <> '')
  AND repository IS NULL;
```

### 000015_services_repository_ref.down.sql
```sql
ALTER TABLE services
  DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS repository;
```

- Do NOT add index on repository JSONB (no query path needs it)
- Backfill is safe for rows with empty repo_url
- Rollback preserves repo_url column

title: Workflow coordinator polls with context.Background() - goroutine leak on shutdown
description:
## Problem
In `internal/workflow/coordinator.go:113`:
```go
go c.pollForCompletion(context.Background(), run.ID, jobEventID)
```

This spawns a goroutine with context.Background() that can block for up to jobTimeout (default 30 minutes). When the application shuts down, these goroutines are NOT cancelled and will leak.

Additionally, there's no tracking of active goroutines, so the graceful shutdown in app.go has no way to wait for them.

## Impact
- Goroutine leak on every deployment that hasn't completed polling
- Graceful shutdown doesn't wait for in-flight deployments
- Deployment status may never be recorded if shutdown during polling

## Required Fix
- Pass a cancellable context derived from the app lifecycle
- Track active poll goroutines with sync.WaitGroup
- Cancel polling on shutdown and mark runs as 'unknown' status
- Add timeout handling at the coordinator level
close_reason: Fixed goroutine leak: Coordinator now owns a cancellable context and sync.WaitGroup for tracking poll goroutines. Shutdown(timeout) cancels context and waits for completion with bounded timeout. Poll goroutines use the coordinator's lifecycle context instead of context.Background(). On cancellation, a detached 5s-timeout context is used to mark runs as timed out (so run state is never left dangling). Also fixed reconciler: moved from context.Background() in New() to the signal context in Run(), so it properly stops on shutdown. Added 10 tests including race-detector-clean concurrency tests.

title: State updates silently swallowed in service layer with _ = err
description:
## Problem
Critical state mutations have their errors silently discarded throughout registry.go:

1. Line 280: `_ = s.intents.UpdateStatus(ctx, dr.DeploymentIntentID, domain.IntentStatusDeploying)` - Creating a run silently ignores intent status update failure
2. Line 317: `_ = s.intents.UpdateStatus(ctx, dr.DeploymentIntentID, intentStatus)` - Completing a run silently ignores intent status update
3. Line 325: `_ = s.state.Upsert(ctx, state)` - Successful deployment state update silently ignored
4. Line 249: `if err := s.state.Upsert(ctx, state); err != nil { s.logger.Error(...) }` - Logs error but returns success to caller

In workflow/coordinator.go:
5. Line 127: `_ = c.registry.CompleteDeploymentRun(ctx, runID, domain.RunStatusTimeout, nil)` - Timeout completion failure silently ignored

## Impact
Deployment state can become inconsistent:
- Intent shows 'pending' while run is 'succeeded'
- State table shows old artifact while intent shows new one deployed
- Operators see contradictory information

## Required Fix
- Return or handle all errors from state mutations
- Use transactions where atomicity matters (intent + state updates)
- At minimum, log errors instead of discarding them entirely
close_reason: Fixed all silent error swallowing: 3 patterns in CompleteDeploymentRun (intent UpdateStatus, intent GetByID, state Upsert), 2 in RecordObservation (state Get, artifact GetByID), 1 in coordinator pollForCompletion. All now return errors or log with structured context. Added 6 new tests verifying error propagation with injectable mock errors.

title: Tests only cover helpers - zero coverage of business logic and handlers
description:
## Problem
The test suite is extremely superficial:

1. **handlers_test.go**: Only tests writeJSON, writeError, decodeJSON, queryInt helper functions. Zero tests for any actual handler (CreateService, RegisterBuild, CreateDeploymentIntent, etc.)
2. **models_test.go**: Only verifies enum string constants are non-empty. No model behavior tests.
3. **events_test.go**: Tests the in-process pub/sub mechanics. Decent but limited.
4. **middleware_test.go**: Tests middleware plumbing, not auth behavior.
5. **config_test.go**: Tests defaults and DSN formatting. Fine but minimal.
6. **integration/registry_test.go**: Only tests service CRUD, skipped unless BAHIA_TEST_DB=1. Doesn't test builds, artifacts, deployments, rollbacks, drift detection, or any complex flow.

## What's Not Tested
- No handler-level HTTP tests with mock registries
- No RegistryService unit tests (the core 500-line business logic file)
- No workflow coordinator tests  
- No reconciler tests
- No Loom client tests
- No Docker observer tests
- No rollback flow tests
- No deployment intent approval/rejection tests
- No drift detection logic tests

## Required Fix
- Add RegistryService unit tests with mock repositories
- Add handler integration tests with httptest
- Add workflow coordinator tests with mock Loom client
- Add reconciler tests with mock observer
- Replace time.Sleep-based event tests with proper synchronization
close_reason: Added 18 HTTP integration tests in router/router_test.go covering the full API surface via httptest. Tests exercise: health/ready endpoints, full service CRUD (create/get/list/update/delete + 404 after delete), environment CRUD, build lifecycle (register/get/status update/list), artifact registration + get + list, full deployment flow (intent→run→complete with auto-approval on non-protected env), protected environment approval flow (pending→approve, double-approve rejection), rejection flow (reject→run fails on rejected intent), state endpoints (list all, list drifted), observation recording with state update, and 404s for non-existent builds/artifacts/intents/runs. title: No input validation on API handlers - accepts any garbage data
description:
## Problem
API handlers accept and persist arbitrary invalid data. Examples:

1. **CreateService** (services.go:20): No validation that Name is non-empty, no uniqueness check before INSERT (relies only on DB constraint), no URL format validation on RepoURL
2. **RegisterBuild** (builds.go:20): No validation that ServiceID references an existing service, GitSHA format not checked, Status not validated against allowed values
3. **RegisterArtifact** (artifacts.go:20): No validation that BuildID or ServiceID exist, image digest format not validated (should be sha256:hex)
4. **CompleteRun** (deployments.go:179): Accepts any string as Status - no validation against allowed DeploymentRunStatus values
5. **CreateDeploymentIntent**: Does validate referenced entities (good), but does NOT validate SourceKind against allowed values
6. **RecordObservation** (state.go:77): No validation at all on health_status or source values

## Impact
Bad data can corrupt the registry state, cause panics in downstream processing, and make drift detection unreliable.

## Required Fix
- Add validation functions per domain type (ValidateBuildStatus, ValidateDigestFormat, etc.)
- Validate all enum-like fields against allowed values before persistence
- Return 400 with specific error messages for validation failures
- Validate foreign key references at service layer before DB insert
close_reason:
Added comprehensive input validation across all API handlers:

- Created domain/validate.go with 10 validator functions (BuildStatus, ScanStatus, SourceKind, DeploymentRunStatus, HealthStatus, RuntimeType, DeployStrategy, ImageDigest sha256 format, GitSHA hex format, RequiredUUID, RequiredString)
- Created domain/validate_test.go with 11 validator tests covering valid/invalid cases
- Updated all 7 handler files (services, builds, artifacts, deployments, environments, state) to validate inputs before processing
- Created handlers/validation_test.go with 18 tests proving bad input returns 400 with descriptive errors
- Total test count: 45 → 76 (+31 tests)

title: Harbor client is created but never used - dead integration
description:
## Problem
In `internal/app/app.go` line 93, the Harbor client is created but immediately discarded:
```go
_ = harbor.NewClient(cfg.Harbor, logger)
```
The Harbor client has real methods (ResolveTag, ImageExists, GetArtifact) but nothing in the codebase calls them.

## Impact
- Artifacts are registered via API with user-supplied digests but never verified against Harbor
- No image existence validation before deployment
- No scan status verification from Harbor before allowing deploys
- The entire Harbor adapter is dead code that creates false confidence

## Required Fix
- Wire Harbor client into RegistryService or a new ArtifactVerifier
- Validate image digest exists in Harbor when registering artifacts
- Optionally verify scan status before allowing deployment intents
- Add config option to skip Harbor verification in dev mode
close_reason: Harbor client is no longer dead code. Added ImageVerifier interface to service layer with Harbor adapter (verifier.go) and NoopImageVerifier for dev/test. RegisterArtifact now verifies images against the container registry: checks existence, cross-validates digest, and adopts scan status from Harbor. Added Harbor.Enabled config flag (default false for backward compat). Wired through app.go — Harbor client is created and used when enabled, noop when disabled. Added 8 new tests: 2 for parseImageRepo, 6 for verification flows (pass, reject non-existent, digest mismatch, verifier error, scan status adoption, noop verifier).

title: DNS web control-plane panels mediated by Nostr events

Extend the DNS web page with human operator controls for zone create/reconcile, policy apply, record override, and drift remediation. Actions must use the web Nostr DNS control-plane client and display request id, publish OK summary, status progress, final result, rejection/errors, and operator pubkey/auth state.

UX should make it clear that changes are signed Nostr commands handled asynchronously by Bahia's control plane. Avoid REST writes and avoid timeout-based done logic.

Tests should cover form validation, command dispatch payloads/tags, result rendering, and error rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Human operators can submit DNS control-plane actions from the web UI via signed Nostr events; UI reflects status/result events; no REST write calls are used; tests verify forms and event-driven lifecycle rendering.
close_reason: Implemented DNS Nostr command panels, tests, and PSTF verification

title: FIPS mesh dashboard tab in DNS/operator UI
description:
Add a FIPS/Mesh tab or panel to the DNS operator UI showing mesh-connected workers/endpoints, overlay addresses, npub identifiers, transport endpoints, mesh health (RTT/loss/jitter/goodput), DNS/FIPS hostnames, and projection/gating status. Data must come from the Web Nostr FIPS mesh read-model store and existing DNS endpoint read models, not new REST endpoints.

UX should include filters for health, worker, capability, and mesh projection state, plus empty/error states for disabled or unavailable FIPS config.

Tests should cover rendering healthy/degraded/unhealthy mesh nodes, tombstone removal, and filter behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The web UI exposes FIPS mesh visibility alongside DNS tools; data is sourced from Nostr read models; health/gating/projection state is understandable to operators; tests cover key render states and filters.

title: Web Nostr FIPS mesh read-model store
description:
Create a browser-side FIPS mesh read-model store that derives mesh nodes and mesh endpoints from Nostr read models, primarily kind 31976 DNSEndpointState events with family=mesh / mesh=fips tags plus worker state events (32000 and legacy-compatible where useful). The store should bootstrap via EOSE, keep a live subscription open, dedupe replaceable events by d tag/pubkey, ignore tombstones, and expose filtering helpers for mesh health and overlay address visibility.

No new REST endpoint should be added for FIPS nodes or health.

Tests should inject EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED paths through the Nostr client abstraction and verify dedupe, tombstone handling, mesh-only filtering, and health classification.
acceptance_criteria: FIPS mesh nodes/endpoints are available to the web UI from Nostr read models only; backfill uses EOSE and live updates use subscriptions; deleted/tombstoned state is handled; deterministic tests cover event ingestion and health classification.
close_reason: Implemented browser-side Nostr FIPS mesh read-model store with EOSE bootstrap, live subscription handling, deterministic tests, PSTF artifacts, and passing web verification.

title: MCP FIPS mesh tools and resources

Add tools/resources such as bahia_fips_list_mesh_nodes and bahia_fips_mesh_status (exact names may follow existing MCP naming conventions) backed by existing worker/DNS projector state. Resources should make mesh-reachable endpoints discoverable with bahia://fips/... or equivalent URIs and metadata including worker pubkey, npub/overlay address, transport endpoints, mesh health, DNS FQDN, and projection status.

All read surfaces must come from persisted/domain/projected Bahia state, not fake data.

Tests should verify tools/list, tools/call, resources/list behavior, empty-state behavior, and filtering to FIPS/mesh records only.
acceptance_criteria: Agent operators can discover FIPS mesh nodes/status via MCP tools/resources; returned data is real projected/persisted state; resources/list includes mesh resources when configured; tests cover populated and empty states.

title: Web Nostr DNS control-plane client and run tracker
description:
Create a browser-side DNS control-plane module/store that publishes signed DNS request events (5941 zone create, 5942 policy apply, 5943 record override, 5944 drift remediate) using existing Nostr helpers and tracks status/result events (6941/7941-7944) by request event id. This is the foundation for web UI DNS writes and must not call REST write endpoints.

Implementation notes:
- Add constants for DNS kinds to web Nostr client/module where appropriate.
- Use publishRequest plus subscribeStatus/awaitResult or equivalent event-driven subscriptions.
- Surface OK acceptance/rejection, status events, result event payloads, CLOSED/AUTH errors, and request id to callers.
- Terminal completion must come from explicit result events, not local timers. Abort/cancel is allowed as user cancellation only.

Tests should cover payload construction, tag normalization/correlation, successful result, rejected publish, and auth/closed subscription errors with deterministic injected events.
acceptance_criteria: Web code can publish all four DNS control-plane commands as signed Nostr events; result tracking is event-driven and correlated by #e/request id; no REST write path is introduced; deterministic tests cover success and rejection paths.
notes: Implemented browser DNS Nostr command module and DNS store run tracker. Verification: npm run test:unit -- --run tests/unit/dns-controlplane.test.js tests/unit/dns-store-commands.test.js tests/unit/controlplane-requests.test.js passed (15 tests); npm run build passed with unrelated pre-existing Svelte warnings. PSTF artifacts added under pstf/features/bahia-5l4f.
close_reason: Implemented and verified DNS browser control-plane client/run tracker

title: DNS/FIPS Nostr-native operator UX
description:
Expose the completed DNS orchestration and FIPS mesh integration to human and agent operators without adding REST write paths. Operators should inspect DNS/FIPS state and submit control-plane actions through signed Nostr events, with web UI affordances and MCP agent tools aligned to Bahia's Nostr-native architecture.

Scope:
- Web UI control plane for DNS zone creation, policy apply, record override, drift remediation via Nostr request/result events.
- Web UI FIPS/mesh visibility using Nostr read models, not new REST endpoints.
- MCP agent tools/resources for FIPS mesh status and node discovery.
- PSTF verification and docs updated for operator UX.

Out of scope:
- New REST write endpoints.
- Bahia acting as DNS resolver/daemon.
- Polling/timeout-based completion semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when all child beads are closed, tests pass, PSTF artifacts document the UX acceptance criteria, and git status is clean/up-to-date with origin.
close_reason: DNS/FIPS Nostr-native operator UX implemented: MCP FIPS tools/resources, Nostr-backed DNS dashboard, Nostr DNS command panels, FIPS mesh UI, resolver Nostr correctness fix, and PSTF/docs rollup all closed and verified.

Intended behavior: Bahia should own backup orchestration, signed Nostr provenance, policy, scheduling, recipes, verification, restore workflows, read models, and observability while delegating repository formats, deduplication, snapshotting, delta transfer, compression, and encryption primitives to battle-tested backends such as Kopia, Velero, ZFS/Btrfs/LVM/Ceph/CSI/Longhorn/Proxmox, Restic, and Borg.

Acceptance criteria:
- PSTF feature artifacts define Bahia as a backup control plane, not a backup engine.
- Event kinds, scoped tags, and command/result/read-model semantics are documented as Nostr-native subscriptions/events rather than polling/RPC.
- Backend adapter boundaries require real publish/OK verification, inbound event validation, CLOSED/AUTH handling, dedupe, idempotency, and verification-first workflows.
- Out-of-scope backup-engine responsibilities are explicitly excluded.
- Follow-up implementation slices are tracked in Beads before code changes.

Verification notes: Initial work should be documentation/PSTF only unless a narrow implementation slice is separately claimed.
design: Control-plane-first design: Backup Recipes + Nostr Events -> Backup Runtime Adapters -> Kopia/Velero/native snapshot tools -> S3/MinIO/local/remote sites. Kopia is the preferred generic backend abstraction; Velero is orchestrated for Kubernetes rather than replaced.
acceptance_criteria: PSTF feature artifacts exist for backup control-plane orchestration; responsibilities are split between Bahia orchestration/provenance and external backup engines; Nostr event semantics and deterministic test expectations are captured; follow-up implementation work is tracked.
notes: PSTF artifacts added under pstf/features/BACKUP_CONTROL_PLANE_ORCHESTRATION. Follow-up issues created: bahia-u4b0 for namespace allocation and bahia-jw8b for first Kopia-backed vertical slice. Namespace conflicts recorded in HITL decisions: 31200 already used for signing attestation; 38395/38396 already documented as AI/ML result kinds.

title: Reconcile dormant WorkerCatalogService payment/stats paths with app wiring
description:
## Problem
The legacy WorkerCatalogService exposes discovery, payment preparation/recording, wallet balances, and job stats APIs, but the main app appears to wire deployment flow around WorkerPolicyService and repository handlers instead. This risks product/API surfaces that look implemented while stats/payment behavior is dormant or inconsistent.

## Evidence
- internal/service/worker_catalog.go defines WorkerCatalogService with Start/Stop/cache refresh, PreparePayment, RecordPayment, GetWorkerStats, RecordJobCompletion, wallet balance helpers, and tests.
- internal/workflow/coordinator.go has WithWorkerCatalog and recordJobStats, but internal/app/app.go constructs the coordinator with WithWorkerPolicy and WithRuntimeResolver only; WithWorkerCatalog is not passed, so coordinator job completions do not update WorkerCatalogService stats.
- internal/app/app.go constructs PaymentService directly and fails closed for cashu.enabled=true; router exposes workers from repository via WorkerHandler and payments via PaymentService, not WorkerCatalogService payment/stats surfaces.
- Existing bahia-pqc, bahia-4jc, and bahia-7yp tracked implementation of discovery/payments/stats/reputation, but not whether this catalog service path is currently wired into app core flow. Cashu live token unsupported is already tracked by bahia-ig2d/bahia-j7ww and should not be duplicated here.

## Scope
Audit current intended architecture for worker catalog, payment, and stats flows. Either wire the WorkerCatalogService paths into app/runtime/API where they are product behavior, or deprecate/remove/guard dormant APIs so the app does not advertise inactive behavior. Do not duplicate Cashu mint-backed-token work already tracked elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented decision identifies the canonical worker catalog/payment/stats path.
- Deployment job completions update the canonical stats path, or stats APIs are removed/guarded as unavailable.
- Payment-preparation APIs either route through the canonical PaymentService/live Cashu boundary or are explicitly disabled/deprecated.
- Tests prove the app wiring exercises the canonical path and cannot silently leave stats/payment surfaces dormant.
acceptance_criteria:
- App wiring either passes/starts the canonical worker catalog service or removes/guards the legacy surface.
- Worker stats exposed by APIs reflect actual deployment completions when enabled.
- Payment/catalog APIs do not imply live Cashu token support beyond bahia-ig2d/bahia-j7ww scope.

title: Remove or harden raw Loom worker discovery subscription path to shared Nostr trust boundary
description:
Problem
The Loom worker discovery subscription path appears to bypass shared Nostr subscription/validation semantics and may have a reconnect-loop control-flow bug, but current runtime reachability needs confirmation.

Evidence
- Oracle audit export: prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-05-16-165809-bahia-inheritance-au-3c11.md, Finding 5.
- internal/adapters/loom/discovery.go uses RelayPool.Subscribe(...) rather than merged SubscribeAllWithEOSE(...).
- It does not call shared ValidateInboundEvent(...).
- The inner break on a closed event channel appears to exit the select rather than the outer loop.
- Selected internal/app/app.go did not show current wiring, so active production reachability is unknown.

Impact
- If active, worker catalog input may be single-relay, unvalidated, and reconnect-fragile.
- If dormant, unsafe code may be reused later without trust-boundary parity.

Scope
- First validate whether WorkerDiscovery is instantiated or reachable in current production composition.
- If active, migrate discovery to shared validation and merged subscription metadata handling, and fix reconnect-on-closed behavior.
- If inactive, remove, quarantine, or document it so it is not reused as an unsafe pattern.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Current WorkerDiscovery runtime reachability is documented with code evidence. 2. Any active discovery path uses shared inbound validation and relay metadata handling. 3. Reconnect behavior resubscribes correctly and cannot spin on a closed event channel. 4. Tests prove the chosen active/hardened or inactive/quarantined behavior.
