title: Honor telemetry config and stop advertising non-existent OTLP setup
description:
## Problem
Telemetry wiring ignores config and overstates support. `app.New()` hardcodes telemetry as enabled with service name `bahia`, while the adapter comment explicitly says OTLP exporters are not actually initialized.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/app.go` calls `telemetry.Setup()` with `Enabled: true` and ignores `cfg.Telemetry`.
- `internal/adapters/telemetry/telemetry.go` logs OTLP metadata but states that production exporters are not initialized.

## Why this matters
Operators cannot disable telemetry cleanly, and configuration implies a tracing/export capability the runtime does not actually provide.

## Scope
- Respect `cfg.Telemetry` in app wiring.
- Either implement the advertised exporter behavior or narrow the config/API so it matches reality.
- Add tests for disabled vs enabled config propagation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- App telemetry honors config enablement and endpoint values.
- No code path claims OTLP exporter setup unless it is real.
close_reason: Completed: app telemetry wiring now honors cfg.Telemetry enablement/service name/OTLP endpoint, and telemetry setup explicitly warns that OTLP exporters are not implemented instead of implying support.

- add config gating for operational REST and mount those routes only when explicitly enabled
- apply any needed middleware tightening so compatibility operational routes are not treated as the normal write path
- add/update tests validating the new default behavior

The outcome should be that REST is no longer the default async LLM operational control plane.
design: Prefer not mounting compatibility operational routes when disabled rather than returning a runtime error. Keep changes additive and minimize churn in handler internals. This bucket depends on the canonical Nostr/MCP command surface being present first so callers have a proper replacement path.

title: Implement Soul Factory lifecycle actions
description:
The Soul Factory provisioner (internal/soulfactory/provisioner.go) has stubbed lifecycle methods that just log 'not implemented'.

Need to implement these methods:

1. SuspendSoul(ctx, soulRef, reason):
   - Update Signet policy to block signing for this agent
   - Pause/stop bahia deployments for this service
   - Publish updated kind:31951 event with status=suspended

2. ResumeSoul(ctx, soulRef):
   - Update Signet policy to allow signing
   - Resume bahia deployments
   - Publish kind:31951 with status=active

3. RevokeSoul(ctx, soulRef, reason):
   - Call Signet to permanently revoke keypair
   - Stop and remove bahia deployments
   - Publish kind:31951 with status=revoked

4. RegenerateSoul(ctx, soulRef, newBrief):
   - Load existing soul from relay
   - Run LLM generation with new/updated brief
   - Update kind:31951 with new content
   - Optionally regenerate avatar

5. RedeploySoul(ctx, soulRef):
   - Load soul to get bahia service ID
   - Create new DeploymentIntent to trigger redeployment

File: internal/soulfactory/provisioner.go:250-299
close_reason: Implemented Soul Factory lifecycle actions (SuspendSoul, ResumeSoul, RevokeSoul, RegenerateSoul, RedeploySoul) in provisioner.go. Added SuspendAgent/ResumeAgent to Signet client. Fixed zap/slog logger mismatch in logs_test.go and runtime/logs_test.go.

title: Implement NIP-98 auth for Blossom uploads
description:
The Blossom upload client (internal/adapters/blossom/upload.go) has a createAuthHeader() function that returns empty string with a TODO comment.

Need to implement:
1. Create a kind:27235 Nostr event with:
   - t tag: action (e.g., 'upload')
   - x tag: SHA-256 hash of content
   - u tag: upload URL
   - method tag: 'PUT'
2. Sign the event with Bahia's private key (or via Signet if available)
3. Base64-encode the signed event
4. Return 'Nostr <base64-encoded-event>' as the Authorization header

This enables authenticated uploads to Blossom servers that require NIP-98.

title: No rate limiting on any API endpoint
description:
## Problem
There is no rate limiting on any API endpoint. The router uses chi middleware for request ID, logging, recovery, CORS, and content-type, but no rate limiter.

## Impact
- API is vulnerable to DoS attacks
- Nostr relay connections can be exhausted by rapid deployment requests
- Database connection pool can be saturated
- Reconciler can be overwhelmed by rapid state changes

## Required Fix
- Add per-IP rate limiting middleware
- Add per-endpoint rate limits (stricter for write operations)
- Add deployment rate limiting (max N deployments per service per time window)
- Consider using chi middleware or tollbooth
close_reason: Added per-IP token bucket rate limiter middleware (no external deps). Read endpoints get 100 req/min, write endpoints get 30 req/min, with separate limiters so exhausting writes doesn't block reads. Includes rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After), automatic stale-entry cleanup, and Stop() for graceful shutdown. 10 tests covering burst limits, per-IP isolation, token replenishment, concurrency, cleanup, and HTTP middleware behavior. Race-detector clean.

title: Config DSN embeds password in URL without escaping - injection risk
description:
## Problem
`internal/config/config.go` DSN() method:
```go
func (c DBConfig) DSN() string {
    return fmt.Sprintf(
        "postgres://%s:%s@%s:%d/%s?sslmode=%s",
        c.User, c.Password, c.Host, c.Port, c.Name, c.SSLMode,
    )
}
```

If the password contains special URL characters (@, :, /, ?, #, etc.), the DSN becomes malformed and connection fails with cryptic errors. Passwords loaded from environment variables commonly contain these characters.

## Required Fix
- Use url.UserPassword() and url.URL for proper escaping
- Or use pgx key=value format instead of URL format
- Add test with special characters in password
close_reason: Replaced fmt.Sprintf DSN construction with net/url.URL builder. User and password are now properly escaped via url.UserPassword(), so special characters (@, :, /, #, ?) no longer break the connection string. Added 7 table-driven test cases covering all problematic characters, each verifying both correct escaping and round-trip parseability.

title: Update handlers don't verify resource existence - silent no-ops
description:
## Problem
The Update methods in pg_service.go and pg_environment.go use UPDATE ... WHERE id=$1 without checking if any rows were affected:
```go
_, err := r.pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE services SET ... WHERE id=$1`, ...)
```

pgx Exec returns a CommandTag with RowsAffected(), but it's ignored. If the ID doesn't exist, the update silently succeeds with 0 rows affected.

Similarly, DeleteService returns success even if the ID doesn't exist.

## Impact
- PUT /api/v1/services/{id} returns 200 even for non-existent IDs
- DELETE /api/v1/services/{id} returns 200 for non-existent IDs
- Clients have no way to know if their update actually changed anything

## Required Fix
- Check RowsAffected() and return ErrNotFound if 0
- Return 404 from handlers when resource doesn't exist
close_reason: Added repository.ErrNotFound sentinel error. All 7 Update/Delete methods across pg_service, pg_environment, pg_build, and pg_deployment now check RowsAffected() and return ErrNotFound when the target row doesn't exist. Handlers for Delete (service, environment), UpdateStatus (build), Approve/Reject (intent), and CompleteRun now map ErrNotFound to HTTP 404. Added 4 router integration tests verifying 404 on delete/update of non-existent services and environments. All mock repos updated to match.

title: Delete operations don't check for dependent resources - cascade risks
description:
## Problem
DeleteService and DeleteEnvironment in the handlers perform a direct DB delete without checking for dependent resources at the application level. While the DB has ON DELETE CASCADE, this means:

1. Deleting a service silently deletes all its builds, artifacts, deployment intents, deployment runs, observations, and state
2. Deleting an environment silently deletes all deployment intents, runs, observations and state for that environment
3. No confirmation, no soft-delete, no audit trail
4. The API returns success with no indication of what was cascaded

## Impact
Accidental deletion of a service wipes its entire deployment history with no recovery path (no soft-delete).

## Required Fix
- Add soft-delete (deleted_at timestamp) instead of hard delete
- Check for active deployments before allowing delete
- Return count of cascaded records in the response
- Add force flag for hard deletes of services with history
close_reason: Implementation complete, build and tests pass

title: Loom client connects/disconnects per relay per operation - no connection pooling
description:
## Problem
Both SubmitJob and PollJobStatus in `internal/adapters/loom/client.go` create a new relay connection for every operation:
```go
relay, err := nostr.RelayConnect(ctx, relayURL)
// ... use once ...
relay.Close()
```

Similarly in nostr/publisher.go, publishEvent creates a new connection for every event publication across every relay.

## Impact
- Each deployment creates N relay connections (N = number of relays)
- Each reconcile cycle that detects drift creates more connections
- Connection overhead dominates small operations
- Risk of rate limiting by relays

## Required Fix
- Maintain persistent relay connections with reconnection logic
- Share connection pool between Loom client and Nostr publisher
- Add connection health monitoring
close_reason: Implementation complete, build and tests pass

title: CORS middleware allows all origins - wildcard * in production
description:
## Problem
`internal/api/middleware/logging.go` CORS function unconditionally sets:
```go
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS")
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Accept, Authorization, Content-Type, X-Request-ID")
```

## Impact
Any website can make authenticated API calls on behalf of a logged-in user (if auth is ever implemented). Combined with the no-op auth, this is an open door.

## Required Fix
- Make CORS origins configurable via config
- Default to restrictive origins in production
- Support credentials mode properly
close_reason: Replaced hardcoded wildcard CORS with configurable origin allowlist. New CORSConfig in config.go accepts AllowedOrigins list (empty = block all cross-origin, secure default). Middleware echoes matching origin with Vary header, sets Max-Age for preflight caching, and silently drops CORS headers for disallowed origins. 8 tests covering allowed/disallowed/wildcard/empty/preflight/no-origin/multi-origin scenarios.

title: Repository layer silently swallows errors on JSON marshal/unmarshal
description:
## Problem
Throughout the repository layer, JSON marshal errors are silently discarded:

pg_build.go:32: `metaJSON, _ := json.Marshal(b.Metadata)`
pg_build.go:59: `_ = json.Unmarshal(metaJSON, &b.Metadata)`
pg_artifact.go:32: `metaJSON, _ := json.Marshal(a.Metadata)`
pg_deployment.go:38-39: `approvalJSON, _ := json.Marshal(di.ApprovalMetadata)`
pg_environment.go:34-35: `selectorJSON, _ := json.Marshal(env.LoomWorkerSelector)`
pg_observation.go:36: `metaJSON, _ := json.Marshal(obs.Metadata)`

## Impact
- If Metadata contains non-serializable types (channels, functions), the error is silently eaten and NULL/empty JSON stored
- On read, corrupt JSON silently returns zero-value metadata
- Data loss is invisible - no logs, no errors, no way to detect it

## Required Fix
- Return errors from Marshal operations or log them
- Validate Metadata types at the service layer before repository calls
- At minimum, log warnings on unmarshal failures
close_reason: Created shared marshalJSON/unmarshalJSON helpers in json_helpers.go. Fixed all 10 marshal and 17 unmarshal patterns across 5 pg_*.go files to return errors instead of silently discarding them. Added 8 unit tests covering valid, nil, empty, invalid, and null-literal cases. All 126 tests pass.

title: Telemetry setup is a placeholder - no tracing or metrics
description:
## Problem
`internal/adapters/telemetry/telemetry.go` is an 11-line file that logs 'telemetry setup (placeholder)' and does nothing. No OpenTelemetry SDK initialization, no OTLP exporter, no tracing, no metrics.

## Evidence
The entire Setup() function is:
```go
func Setup(logger *zap.Logger) {
    logger.Info("telemetry setup (placeholder)")
    // TODO: Initialize OpenTelemetry SDK with OTLP exporter.
}
```

## Impact
Zero observability in production. No distributed tracing across Loom/Nostr/Harbor calls. No metrics on API latency, deployment success rates, drift detection timing, etc.

## Required Fix
- Initialize OpenTelemetry SDK with OTLP exporter
- Add tracing middleware to HTTP router
- Instrument key operations (deploy, reconcile, Loom submit)
- Export metrics (request duration, deployment count, drift count)
- Make telemetry endpoint configurable
close_reason: Implementation complete, build and tests pass

title: DNS record override persistence and durable zone commands
description:
Make DNSRecordOverride (kind 5943) and DNSZoneCreate (kind 5941) durable. Currently these return 'unsupported' in Phase 1 because DNS runtime is config-backed.

1. DNS Zone persistence: Add DNSZoneRepository interface. DB migration for dns_zones table. Update buildDNSRuntime() to merge config zones with DB zones. Make DNSZoneCreate handler create/update zones in DB.

2. Record override persistence: Add DNSOverrideRepository. DB migration for dns_record_overrides table. Override model: signed operator request pins a record that the projector won't overwrite. Overrides should be marked source='manual_override' in endpoint state. Projector must check overrides before deriving records. DNSRecordOverride handler persists override and triggers reconcile.

3. Backend interface expansion: Add optional UpsertRecord/DeleteRecord methods (or a separate RecordMutator interface) for backends that support granular operations. CoreDNS adapter can support this via individual etcd key writes.

Files: internal/repository/dns.go (new interfaces), internal/db/migrations/ (new), internal/controlplane/dns_handlers.go (modify), internal/reconcile/dns_projector.go (override checking), internal/app/app.go (wire repos). Design doc: §10.4, §5.1.

title: Hardware-aware DNS and SRV record support
description:
Extend DNS projection with two capabilities:

1. Hardware-aware DNS: Generate hardware-specific DNS entries from worker accelerator topology. Examples:
- rk3588.edge.cascadia → local NPU runtime
- l40s.gpu.cascadia → L40S GPU workers
- a100.gpu.cascadia → A100 GPU workers
Worker.Accelerators and Worker.MLCapabilities already provide the data source.

2. SRV record support: Design doc Rule 3 specifies ML inference endpoints should project SRV records alongside A records. Phase 0/1 only project A/AAAA/CNAME. Add DNSRecordTypeSRV to domain types. Extend projector to emit SRV records with Priority, Weight, Port fields from DNSRecord. Extend backend adapters to handle SRV payloads.

Files: internal/domain/dns.go (add SRV type, extend DNSRecord with Priority/Weight/Port), internal/reconcile/dns_projector.go (modify), internal/adapters/dns/coredns.go (SRV key format), internal/adapters/dns/filesystem.go (SRV serialization). Design doc: §6.2 Rule 3-4, §8.3.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split-horizon zone filtering and capability-based alias records
description:
Implement two advanced projection features:

1. Split-horizon: Zone visibility gates which endpoints appear in which zones. Internal endpoints should not be projected to external zones. Edge endpoints should only appear in edge-scoped zones. The projector should filter endpoints by zone visibility after policy evaluation.

2. Capability-based alias records (design doc Rule 5): When policy enables capability routing, generate additional CNAME alias records like:
- llm.prod.cascadia → CNAME → drydock-review.prod.cascadia
- speech.local.cascadia → A → nearest edge runtime with speech capability
- gpu.edge.cascadia → A → nearest online worker with GPU

Config flag: dns.projection.capability_aliases (already reserved in config).

Files: internal/reconcile/dns_projector.go (modify), internal/reconcile/dns_projector_test.go (add tests), internal/config/config.go (use existing flag). Design doc: §6.2 Rule 5, §8.1, §8.2.
close_reason: Closed

title: DNS policy evaluation engine in projector
description:
Integrate policy evaluation into the DNS projector pipeline. After materializing DNSEndpoints and before deriving DNSRecords, apply matching policies to filter, transform, and route endpoints. Policy evaluation order: zone-scoped policies first, then global. Rule matching: AND within a rule (all match criteria must pass), first-match-wins across rules within a policy.

Behaviors:
- Visibility override: endpoint re-routed to a different zone based on policy match
- TTL override: per-endpoint TTL changed from zone default
- WeightBias: SRV weight adjusted for matched endpoints
- Exclude: matched endpoints suppressed from DNS projection entirely

Add DNSPolicySource interface to projector. Projector applies policies between ListDNSEndpoints and ProjectZoneRecords.

Files: internal/reconcile/dns_projector.go (modify), internal/reconcile/dns_projector_test.go (add policy tests). Design doc: §6.2 Rule 5, §8.2.
close_reason: Closed

title: DNS policy domain types, validation, and persistence
description:
Add DNSPolicy, DNSPolicyRule, DNSPolicyMatch, DNSPolicyAction domain types to internal/domain/dns.go with validation. Create repository interfaces (DNSPolicyRepository) in internal/repository/dns.go. Add DB migration for dns_policies table. This is the foundation for all policy work — split-horizon, TTL overrides, exclusion rules, and weighted routing all depend on these types.

Design doc reference: §4.4 DNS policy types. Fields: ID, Name, ZoneID (optional scope), EnvironmentID (optional), Rules []DNSPolicyRule, Enabled, Metadata. Match criteria: Capabilities, Hardware, Geohash (prefix), Environment, Runtime. Actions: Visibility override, TTL override, WeightBias, Exclude.

Files: internal/domain/dns.go (add types), internal/domain/dns_test.go (validation tests), internal/repository/dns.go (new), internal/db/migrations/ (new migration).

title: Nostr event log table (nostr_events) is never written to
description:
## Problem
The migration creates a `nostr_events` table for audit trail:
```sql
CREATE TABLE nostr_events (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind INTEGER NOT NULL,
  ...
);
```

But no code in the entire codebase writes to this table. The Nostr publisher publishes events to relays but never records them locally. The Loom client receives events but never persists them.

## Impact
- No audit trail of Nostr events published or received
- No ability to replay or verify what was broadcast
- Table exists but is permanently empty

## Required Fix
- Record published events in nostr_events table
- Record received DVM result events
- Add query endpoint for audit trail
close_reason: Implementation complete, build and tests pass

title: Nostr-native DNS resolution from kind 31976 events
description:
Enable Nostr clients to resolve endpoints purely from kind 31976 DNSEndpointState events without traditional DNS. This makes the Nostr relay itself a service discovery mechanism.

Design:
- Client subscribes to kind 31976 with author=bahia-pubkey
- Filters by tags: env, capability, runtime, health
- Builds a local endpoint cache from replaceable events
- Resolves service names to addresses by matching d-tag coordinates

Provide a reference client library (Go or TypeScript) that:
1. Connects to configured relay(s)
2. Subscribes to kind 31976
3. Maintains a local endpoint map
4. Exposes a Resolve(name, env) → (address, port, metadata) API
5. Handles tombstones (deleted=true events)
6. Supports capability-based queries ('find me an llm endpoint in prod')

This is the long-term vision: DNS as a derived view of the Nostr event graph, resolvable without any DNS server at all.

Files: pkg/discovery/ or cmd/dns-resolver/ (new reference client). Design doc: §16 Q6, §17.
close_reason: Implemented pkg/discovery Resolver for kind 31976 DNSEndpointState events with signed event validation, replaceable-event cache updates, tombstone handling, capability queries, and deterministic unit tests.

title: Investigate /settings route rendering dashboard content in local Playwright dev session
description: During relay/auth verification on 2026-05-10, navigating to http://127.0.0.1:4173/settings in the local Vite/Svelte dev session rendered the dashboard content while retaining the /settings URL. Fix: removed /settings from protected prefixes so relay/auth settings can render before sign-in. Verification: npm run test:unit -- --run tests/unit/route-access.test.js passed; npm run build passed; preview on 127.0.0.1:4174/settings retained /settings and rendered h1 Settings.
